mainTopic: קידושין with property that is not truly the man's own: stolen items and a כהן's share of קרבנות
overview: The גמרא first settles a contradiction about a man who betroths a woman with something he took from her. It works only if they had already arranged the match. Next come three stories brought before רבא: coins grabbed from a stranger, a sharecropper's handful of onions, and a brewer's beer sediment. In each case the betrothal fails, because the owner never truly gave up or allowed use of the item. A ברייתא about separating תרומה without permission shows that the 'go to the better ones' test applies only to תרומה, while the brewer's owner spoke out of embarrassment. A new משנה then rules that a כהן cannot betroth with his share of קרבנות, and records disputes about מעשר שני and הקדש. The גמרא explains that after שחיטה the כהנים eat 'from the table of the Most High' and do not own the meat. A story shows רבי יהודה, סומכוס and רבי יוסי arguing whether the case is even realistic. רבי יוחנן then traces their מחלוקת to one פסוק. The amud ends just as רבי יוחנן begins a new statement.

steps.title: Contradiction: stealing from the woman herself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier ברייתא, which said that if a man grabbed a coin from the woman and betrothed her with it, she is betrothed. The משנה also deals with taking something of hers, yet רב rules she is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the משנה he stole something of hers, and רב says she is not betrothed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. The ברייתא says that betrothing a woman with something taken from her works, but רב rules on the משנה that it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases involve property that originally belonged to the woman. If the ברייתא says she is betrothed, why does רב say she is not? The two rulings seem to clash.

phrases.english: But the משנה, where he stole what was hers,
and רב says: she is not betrothed!
phrases.notes: This clashes with the ברייתא just quoted, which said that if he grabbed a coin from her, she is betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא discussed just before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא ruling that betrothal with an item grabbed from the woman works
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's ruling on the משנה treats a similar case of taking her property as a failed betrothal

steps.title: Answer: did he arrange the match beforehand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא deals with a man who had already arranged the match with her, while the משנה deals with a man who had not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This case is where he had arranged the match, and that case is where he had not arranged it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the two rulings into two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they had already agreed to marry, we assume she is fine with him using her item, so she lets go of her claim and she is betrothed. Without an arrangement, the item is simply stolen, so the betrothal fails.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא allows betrothal with stolen goods in general. It only works because an existing match shows the woman is happy to give up the item.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where he had arranged the match,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the ברייתא, where she is betrothed.

phrases.english: that one is where he had not arranged the match.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings deal with the same situation and contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: With a prior match she gives up the item and is betrothed. Without one, the item is stolen and she is not betrothed.
steps.whatToRemember: Betrothal with an item taken from the woman works only if a prior match shows she willingly gives up her claim.

steps.title: Story: coins grabbed from a third person
steps.stepSummary: A man grabbed coins from someone else, threw them to a woman, and declared her betrothed. The case is brought to רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman was washing her feet in a water vessel. A man came, grabbed coins from his friend, threw them to her, and said: you are betrothed to me. The case came before רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story and sets up a question for רבא. It is preparing for רבא's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the stolen money belongs to a third person, not to the woman. The question is whether the robber owns the coins enough to use them for קידושין.

phrases.english: There was a certain woman
who was washing her feet
in a vessel of water.
A certain man came,
grabbed coins from his fellow,
and threw them to her.
He said to her: you are betrothed to me.
That man came before רבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a series of practical cases on betrothal with property that is not truly his
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is she betrothed with coins that were stolen from a third person?

steps.title: רבא: we assume the owner did not give up
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that no one follows רבי שמעון's view that in an ordinary robbery the owner gives up hope. So the coins still belong to the owner, and she is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: no one is concerned for this view of רבי שמעון, who said that in an ordinary robbery the owner gives up hope.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the case. Since we do not follow רבי שמעון, the robber never owned the coins, so the betrothal does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner had given up hope (יאוש), the robber might own the coins and the betrothal could work. רבא says we do not assume יאוש, so the coins are still the owner's. The woman is not even possibly betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no one who takes into account
The owner's giving up hope of getting it back

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that betrothal with stolen money from a stranger fails, because we do not assume the owner gave up hope.

phrases.english: He said: there is no one who is concerned
for this view of רבי שמעון,
who said: an ordinary robbery,
the owner has given up hope.
phrases.notes: If the owner gave up hope, the robber could own the coins. רבא says we don't assume that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא's ruling on the case in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is not betrothed, because the owner has not given up hope and the coins are still his

steps.title: Sharecropper betroths with a handful of onions
steps.stepSummary: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions from the field he worked. רבא asked him: who gave you permission?
steps.simpleTranslation: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions. He came before רבא. רבא said to him: who allowed you to take them?
steps.whatsHappening: Another story comes before רבא. רבא rules that the onions were not the sharecropper's to take, so the betrothal fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field's produce has not yet been divided, so part of every onion belongs to the landowner. Taking a handful without permission is theft, and stolen goods cannot be used for קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharecropper who works a field for a share of the crop

phrases.english: There was a certain sharecropper
who betrothed a woman with a handful of onions.
He came before רבא.
He said to him: who gave you permission?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second practical case in the same series
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sharecropper who takes a handful of unshared produce without permission has stolen it, and the betrothal fails

steps.title: Limit: a whole bundle is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבא's ruling to a small handful. If the sharecropper took a full bundle, he can tell the owner to take an equal bundle, so it is not theft.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to a handful. But with a bundle, he can say to him: I took a bundle, you take a bundle, bundle for bundle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the ruling in step 5. A full bundle can count as the sharecropper's fair share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a bundle, there is a clear matching portion the owner can take for himself. The sharecropper has simply divided early, so it is not theft. A small handful does not work like this as a share.

phrases.english: And this applies only to a handful,
but with a bundle, he can say to him:
I took a bundle,
you take a bundle,
a bundle for a bundle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking a full bundle counts as taking one's own share, so it is not theft

steps.title: Brewer betroths with beer sediment
steps.stepSummary: A brewer betrothed a woman with sediment from someone else's beer. The owner found him and asked why he didn't give from the sharper, better sediment. The brewer asked רבא whether this meant the owner had agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A brewer betrothed a woman with beer sediment. The owner of the beer came and found him, and said: why don't you give from this sharp one? He came before רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a third case for רבא. The owner's comment raises the question of whether he agreed after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier cases, here the owner seems to approve, even offering a better kind. The question is whether that comment counts as permission that makes the betrothal valid.

phrases.english: There was a certain brewer
who betrothed a woman with sediment of beer.
The owner of the beer came and found him.
He said to him: why don't you give
from this sharp one?
He came before רבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third practical case in the same series
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the owner's comment show approval that makes the betrothal valid?

steps.title: רבא: "go to the better ones" works only for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the rule treating "go take the better ones" as approval applies only to תרומה. Here the owner's comment does not count as permission, so she is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: they said "go to the better ones" only regarding תרומה alone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the brewer. The owner's remark does not turn the sediment into a valid gift, so the betrothal fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תרומה, a person who separates it is doing a מצוה the owner must do anyway, so a remark like this can show real approval. Here the brewer used the sediment for his own benefit, so the owner's comment is not real permission. Step 12 explains that the owner spoke only out of embarrassment.

keyTerms.meaning: Go over to the better ones
The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: In all three stories רבא asks one question: did the owner truly give up or allow the item? If not, the betrothal fails.

phrases.english: He said: they did not say "go to the better ones"
phrases.notes: Someone took another person's things without asking, and the owner told him to take the nicer ones. Sometimes that remark counts as the owner agreeing.

phrases.english: except with regard to תרומה alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אָמְרוּ כְּלָךְ אֵצֶל יָפוֹת אֶלָּא לְעִנְיַן תְּרוּמָה בִּלְבָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא's ruling on the case in step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner's remark counts as approval only for תרומה. Here it is not permission, so she is not betrothed.

steps.title: The source: separating תרומה from someone else's produce
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a person separates תרומה from a friend's field without permission, it counts only if the owner does not see it as robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: When did they say that if someone separates תרומה without the owner knowing, it counts as תרומה? If a person went into his friend's field, gathered produce, and separated תרומה without permission: if the owner treats it as robbery, it is not תרומה. If he does not, it is תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that רבא was relying on in step 8, when he said the rule about the owner's approval applies to תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the basic rule. תרומה separated without permission can still count, but only if the owner does not object and see it as theft. The next lines will explain how we know what the owner thinks.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: As it is taught:
phrases.notes: This is the source for רבא's ruling in step 8 about the owner who said to take the better ones.

phrases.english: When did they say:
One who separates תרומה without the owner's knowledge,
his תרומה is תרומה?
Where one went down into his friend's field
and gathered and separated תרומה without permission,
if he is concerned about it as robbery,
phrases.notes: He means the owner. Does the owner see this as theft?

phrases.english: his תרומה is not תרומה,
and if not, his תרומה is תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא source behind רבא's answer in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the 'go take the better ones' rule is a rule about תרומה

steps.title: How do we know whether the owner minds?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we can tell whether the owner sees the act as robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would he know whether the owner sees it as robbery or not?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a question is asked to set up the next line: how do we find out what the owner really thinks?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 9 depends on the owner's feelings, and feelings are hidden. So the ברייתא needs a clear sign that shows whether the owner minds.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where (how do we know)

phrases.english: And from where would he know

phrases.aramaic: אִם חוֹשֵׁשׁ מִשּׁוּם גָּזֵל אִם לָאו?
phrases.english: whether he is concerned about it as robbery or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to apply the condition set out in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A way to tell whether the owner objects to the תרומה being separated

steps.title: The test: are there really better ones?
steps.stepSummary: If the owner says 'go to the nicer ones' and nicer produce really exists, the תרומה counts. If not, it does not. If the owners were adding more, it counts either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner came, found him, and said: 'Go over to the nicer ones,' then if nicer produce than his is found, his תרומה is תרומה. If not, it is not תרומה. If the owners were gathering and adding more, either way his תרומה is תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. It uses the owner's words and actions as signs of whether he really agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nicer produce really exists, the owner meant what he said, so he agrees. If there is nothing nicer, he was speaking sarcastically, so he objects. If the owners themselves pick more and add to the pile, that clearly shows they agree, whatever they said.

keyTerms.meaning: Go over to the nicer ones

steps.confusionAlert: 'Go to the nicer ones' can mean two opposite things. It may be real approval, or it may be an angry, sarcastic remark. That is why we check whether nicer produce actually exists.

phrases.english: Where the owner came and found him
and said to him: 'Go over to the nicer ones,'
if nicer ones than those are found,
his תרומה is תרומה,
and if not, his תרומה is not תרומה.
If the owners were gathering and adding,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ – תְּרוּמָתוֹ תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: either way, his תרומה is תרומה.
phrases.notes: Whether or not nicer produce is found, adding to the pile shows the owners agree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner agrees if nicer produce really exists or if he adds to the pile. Otherwise his words are sarcastic and the תרומה does not count.

steps.title: The brewer's case is different: the owner was just embarrassed
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that in the brewer's case, the owner's words came from embarrassment, not real agreement, so the woman is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, he did it because of embarrassment, and she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא returns to the brewer's case and explains why the תרומה rule does not apply to it. The woman is not betrothed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תרומה, the owner's words can be trusted as real approval. In the brewer's case, the owner spoke only because he felt too embarrassed to protest at a קידושין. He never truly gave up his sediment. So the brewer used something that was not his, and the קידושין fails.
steps.whatToRemember: Polite-sounding words do not always mean real permission. In the brewer's case they came from embarrassment, so the woman is not betrothed.

phrases.english: But here,
phrases.notes: Back to the brewer who betrothed with someone else's sediment (step 7).

phrases.english: he did it because of embarrassment,
and she is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הָכָא, מִשּׁוּם כִּיסּוּפָא הוּא דַּעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא to the brewer's case and shows why that case is different.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The brewer's קידושין is invalid, because the owner's words came from embarrassment and were not real consent.

steps.title: New משנה: betrothing with a כהן's share of קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who betroths a woman with his share of קרבנות, whether the holiest kind or the lighter kind, does not betroth her.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who betroths with his portion, whether of the holiest offerings or of the lighter offerings, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that a כהן cannot betroth a woman with his share of the קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה covers both levels of holiness, קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים. The ruling is the same for both: the woman is not betrothed. Step 17 explains the reason.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who betroths with his portion,
phrases.notes: This is a כהן using his share of the קרבנות.

phrases.english: whether of the holiest offerings,
or of the lighter offerings,
she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה, separate from the stories about רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothing with a כהן's share of any קרבן, high or light holiness, is not valid.

steps.title: Betrothing with מעשר שני: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says betrothing with מעשר שני never works. רבי יהודה says it fails if done by mistake but works if done on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: With מעשר שני, whether by mistake or on purpose, he has not betrothed her. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: by mistake, he has not betrothed her. On purpose, he has betrothed her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case, מעשר שני, and records a disagreement between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר makes no distinction: the קידושין fails either way. רבי יהודה splits the case by the man's intent. By mistake it fails, and on purpose it works. The גמרא will explain the reasoning behind each view.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's ruling sounds backward: doing it on purpose works, but doing it by mistake does not. Hold that question; the גמרא will explain it.

phrases.english: With second tithe,
whether by mistake or on purpose,
he has not betrothed; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
By mistake, he has not betrothed;
on purpose, he has betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, בֵּין שׁוֹגֵג בֵּין מֵזִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a second kind of holy food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: betrothing with מעשר שני is never valid. רבי יהודה: it is invalid by mistake and valid on purpose.

steps.title: Betrothing with Temple property: on purpose or by mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says betrothing with הקדש works if done במזיד but not בשוגג. רבי יהודה says the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man betroths a woman with Temple property: done on purpose, she is betrothed; done by mistake, she is not betrothed. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says: by mistake, she is betrothed; on purpose, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It gives a מחלוקת about a man who betroths a woman with property that belongs to the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 dealt with מעשר שני. This case is about הקדש. Here רבי מאיר says it works only במזיד, and רבי יהודה says it works only בשוגג. The משנה does not give the reasons here.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that belongs to the Temple
On purpose, knowing what he is doing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. רבי מאיר: on purpose works. רבי יהודה: by mistake works. They are exact opposites.

phrases.english: And with consecrated property,
if on purpose, he has betrothed her;
and if by mistake, he has not betrothed her.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
by mistake, he has betrothed her; on purpose, he has not betrothed her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of holy items used for קידושין, moving from מעשר שני to הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: הקדש works for קידושין במזיד, not בשוגג. רבי יהודה: works בשוגג, not במזיד.

steps.title: Does the משנה go against רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה's ruling about a כהן's share of קדשים קלים disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי, who calls קדשים קלים the owner's money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי יוסי הגלילי? A ברייתא teaches that the words 'and commits a trespass against ה׳' include קדשים קלים, which are the owner's money. This is the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now begins its discussion. It asks whether the משנה's rule in step 13 conflicts with a known opinion of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said a כהן cannot betroth with his share of קדשים קלים, so it seems the share is not his. But רבי יוסי הגלילי says קדשים קלים are 'ממונו', the owner's own money. If they belong to their owner, the כהן's share should belong to him, and his קידושין should work.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test)
To include (learning an extra case from a word in a פסוק)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Shall we say that our משנה
is not in line with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
'and commits a trespass against ה׳':
this comes to include offerings of lesser holiness
which are his own property,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's ruling in step 13 and tests it against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a כהן cannot betroth with his share of קדשים קלים (step 13).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי הגלילי says קדשים קלים are the owner's money. Then the כהן's share should be his, and he should be able to betroth with it.

steps.title: Ownership exists only while the animal is alive
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can even follow רבי יוסי הגלילי. He meant ownership only while the animal is alive. After שחיטה, the כהנים receive their share 'from the table of the Most High'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. When he said this, he meant while the animal is alive, but not after שחיטה. Why? When the כהנים receive their share, they receive it from the table of the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no conflict. רבי יוסי הגלילי was speaking only about a live animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before שחיטה, a קדשים קלים animal counts as its owner's money. After שחיטה, the כהנים do not own the meat. They are like guests eating from ה׳'s table. So the כהן has nothing of his own to give for קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (the משנה still fits that opinion)
The table of the Most High (ה׳'s table)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: what the כהנים eat from קרבנות is something they are allowed to eat, not something they own. That is why it cannot be used for קידושין.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yosei HaGelili;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי – מֵחַיִּים,
phrases.english: when Rabbi Yosei HaGelili said it, he meant while the animal is alive,
but after slaughter, no.
What is the reason?
When they acquire it,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the כהנים who receive their share of the קרבן.

phrases.english: they acquire it from the table of the Most High.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by narrowing what רבי יוסי הגלילי meant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited opinion (alive vs. after שחיטה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי הגלילי's 'ממונו' seemed to cover the כהן's share even after שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ownership applies only to a live animal. After שחיטה, the כהנים eat from ה׳'s table and own nothing they could betroth with.

steps.title: The משנה's wording 'his portion' supports this
steps.stepSummary: The משנה speaks of a כהן betrothing 'with his portion', which is meat received after שחיטה. This supports the answer, and the גמרא concludes 'learn from it'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact. It teaches: one who betroths with his portion, whether קדשי קדשים or קדשים קלים, has not betrothed. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from the exact words of the משנה, then closes with 'שמע מינה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן gets a 'portion' only after the animal is slaughtered. So the משנה is talking only about meat after שחיטה, which fits the answer in step 17. It says nothing against a live animal being its owner's.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact (it supports what was just said)
With his portion (his share of the קרבן)
Learn from it (the point is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן cannot betroth with his share of any קרבן, because after שחיטה he eats 'from the table of the Most High' and does not own it. This fits even רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says קדשים קלים are their owner's money only while alive.

phrases.english: The wording is also exact, since it teaches:
one who betroths with his portion,
phrases.notes: The key word is 'portion', the share a כהן gets after the animal is slaughtered.

phrases.english: whether offerings of the highest holiness
or offerings of lesser holiness,
has not betrothed her.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 17 from the precise language of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the כהן lacks ownership only after שחיטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'המקדש בחלקו', 'with his portion'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה fits רבי יוסי הגלילי, because it deals only with the כהן's portion after שחיטה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה bars רבי מאיר's students, but סומכוס pushes in
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא opens a story: after רבי מאיר died, רבי יהודה told his students to keep רבי מאיר's students out, because they come to argue, not to learn. סומכוס pushed his way in anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: After רבי מאיר passed away, רבי יהודה told his students: Don't let רבי מאיר's students come in here. They are quarrelsome. They don't come to learn תורה; they come to stump me with הלכות. סומכוס pushed his way in and entered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a story. This step sets the scene for the הלכה question that סומכוס is about to raise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story continues our topic of a כהן betrothing with his portion. The scene shows tension between the two בתי מדרש. סומכוס's 'pushing in' matters later, because רבי יוסי will use the same idea of 'pushing in' in his answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Quarrelsome people who argue to pick a fight
To overwhelm me, to beat me down
Pushed his way in and entered

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
After the passing of Rabbi Meir,
Rabbi Yehuda said to his students:

phrases.aramaic: אַל יִכָּנְסוּ תַּלְמִידֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְכָאן,
phrases.english: Do not let Rabbi Meir's students enter here,
because they are quarrelsome,
and they do not come to learn Torah;
rather, they come to overwhelm me with halachos.
Sumchus pushed his way in and entered.
phrases.notes: סומכוס was one of רבי מאיר's students, the very people רבי יהודה wanted kept out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לְאַחַר פְּטִירָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the משנה's case of a כהן betrothing with his portion, the גמרא brings a story where that same question was argued.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: רבי יהודה bars רבי מאיר's students, and סומכוס enters anyway.

steps.title: סומכוס reports that a כהן cannot betroth with his portion
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס says that רבי מאיר taught: a כהן who betroths with his portion of the קרבנות, whether קדשי קדשים or קדשים קלים, has not made a valid betrothal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This is what רבי מאיר taught me: One who betroths with his portion, whether from the most-holy offerings or from the lesser-holy offerings, has not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: סומכוס reports רבי מאיר's ruling. A כהן's portion of any קרבן cannot be used for קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not split between the two levels of קרבנות. Both קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים fail. This ruling is what sets off רבי יהודה's anger in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who betroths with his portion of the קרבנות
Most-holy offerings, eaten only in the עזרה
He has not betrothed; the קידושין do not work

phrases.english: He said to them:
This is what Rabbi Meir taught me:
One who betroths with his portion,
phrases.notes: This is a כהן using his share of the קרבנות, the same case as in our משנה.

phrases.english: whether with most-holy offerings
or with lesser-holy offerings,
has not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: סומכוס, now inside, states the ruling he came with.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a כהן who betroths with his portion of any קרבן has not betrothed.

steps.title: רבי יהודה objects that the case is unrealistic
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gets angry, repeats his warning about רבי מאיר's students, and says the question is pointless: how would a woman even be in the עזרה to receive קדשי קדשים?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה got angry. He said to them: Didn't I tell you not to let רבי מאיר's students in here, because they are quarrelsome and come to stump me, not to learn תורה? Where would a woman be in the עזרה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה attacks the ruling as a made-up case. A woman would not be in the עזרה, where קדשי קדשים must be eaten, so the question never really comes up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשי קדשים may not leave the עזרה. So the betrothal would have to happen there, and רבי יהודה assumes a woman is not found there. He is not answering the הלכה; he is saying the question is not practical.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How would that happen?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda became angry (at them).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: לֹא כָּךְ אָמַרְתִּי לָכֶם:
phrases.english: He said to them: Didn't I tell you this:

phrases.aramaic: אַל יִכָּנְסוּ מִתַּלְמִידֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְכָאן
phrases.english: Do not let any of Rabbi Meir's students enter here
because they are quarrelsome,
and they do not come to learn Torah;
rather, they come to overwhelm me with halachos.
And where would a woman be in the Temple courtyard?!
phrases.notes: קדשי קדשים can only be eaten in the עזרה, and he assumes no woman would be there to receive them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה reacts to סומכוס's ruling by saying the case is not realistic.
steps.kashyaTarget: The relevance of רבי מאיר's ruling about betrothing with קדשי קדשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קדשי קדשים must stay in the עזרה, and a woman is not found there, so the betrothal could never happen.

steps.title: רבי יוסי shows the case can really happen
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי refuses to stay silent. He shows three ways the case is realistic: a father can accept קידושין for his daughter in the עזרה, a woman can send a שליח there, and a woman might push her way in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: People will say: מאיר passed away, יהודה got angry, יוסי kept quiet; what will become of the תורה? Isn't it common for a man to accept קידושין for his daughter in the עזרה? Isn't it common for a woman to appoint a שליח to accept her קידושין in the עזרה? And besides, if she pushed in and entered, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי rejects רבי יהודה's claim that the case is unrealistic. He gives three ways it could happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman does not have to be in the עזרה herself, because her father or her שליח can receive the קידושין for her. And even if she came in where she shouldn't, the law still has to be known. So רבי מאיר's question is a real one.

keyTerms.meaning: Lay down; here it means passed away

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that questions in תורה must be answered seriously. A question can't be pushed aside just because the case seems unusual.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: People will say:

phrases.aramaic: מֵאִיר שָׁכַב, יְהוּדָה כָּעַס, יוֹסֵי שָׁתַק –
phrases.english: Meir passed away, Yehuda got angry, Yosei kept quiet;
what will become of (the words of) the Torah?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: Isn't it common for a man
to accept betrothal for his daughter in the courtyard?

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אִשָּׁה עֲשׂוּיָה לַעֲשׂוֹת לָהּ שָׁלִיחַ
phrases.english: And isn't it common for a woman to appoint an agent for herself
to accept her betrothal in the courtyard?
And furthermore: if she pushed in and entered, what then?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֵין אָדָם עָשׂוּי לְקַבֵּל קִידּוּשִׁין לְבִתּוֹ בַּעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה's claim that the case could not happen.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the case is unrealistic. It does not yet decide the הלכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה assumed the woman herself must be in the עזרה. A father or a שליח can receive for her, and she might push in herself.

steps.title: The מחלוקת: רבי יהודה says betrothed, רבי יוסי says not
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא records the actual מחלוקת: according to רבי יהודה, a woman betrothed with a כהן's portion of קדשי קדשים is betrothed; according to רבי יוסי, she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says: She is betrothed. רבי יוסי says: She is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that states each side's הלכה directly. This sets up רבי יוחנן's explanation of where each opinion comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story, רבי יהודה only called the case unrealistic. Here we learn his actual view: the קידושין work. רבי יוסי, who defended the question, holds like רבי מאיר that they do not work.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the sides. רבי יהודה, who got angry, actually holds the קידושין work. רבי יוסי, who defended the question, holds they do not.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says: She is betrothed;
Rabbi Yosei says: She is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story shows the question is real, the גמרא gives the actual opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: betrothal with a כהן's portion of קדשי קדשים works. רבי יוסי: it does not work.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both learn from the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that both opinions come from one פסוק. רבי יהודה reads 'for you' as 'for all your needs', so קידושין are allowed. רבי יוסי compares the portion to the fire: just as the fire consumes, the portion is only for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned from one פסוק: 'This shall be yours of the most holy things, from the fire.' רבי יהודה holds that 'yours' means for all your needs. רבי יוסי holds it is like the fire: just as the fire's part is for consuming, the כהן's part is also only for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the source for the מחלוקת. He shows how each תנא reads one פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה stresses the word 'לך', which gives the כהן broad rights, including using his portion for קידושין. רבי יוסי stresses 'מן האש' and compares the כהן's part to the altar's part: both are only for eating. If the portion may only be eaten, it can't be used for קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: They both learned from one פסוק
Like the fire of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether a כהן can betroth with his portion of קדשי קדשים depends on one פסוק. 'לך' means for all your needs, so it works (רבי יהודה). 'מן האש' means only for eating, so it does not work (רבי יוסי).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Both of them learned from one verse:

phrases.aramaic: ״זֶה יִהְיֶה לְךָ מִקֹּדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים מִן הָאֵשׁ״.
phrases.english: "This shall be yours of the most holy things, from the fire."
Rabbi Yehuda holds:
"Yours" means for all your needs.
And Rabbi Yosei holds: it is like the fire.
Just as the fire is for consuming,
so too, his portion is also only for eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source behind the מחלוקת stated in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both opinions come from במדבר 18:9. 'לך' means for all needs, so קידושין work (רבי יהודה). 'מן האש' means only for eating, so they do not (רבי יוסי).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement in the name of רבי יוחנן. Only the words 'רבי יוחנן says' appear here. His actual teaching comes in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It tells us that רבי יוחנן is about to teach something, but his words come right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is only an introduction that tells us who is speaking. It gives us no rule, question or proof yet. Wait for the next line to find out what רבי יוחנן adds.

keyTerms.meaning: A statement or teaching given in the name of a specific חכם.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to guess the teaching from this line alone. 'אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן' only names the speaker, and the content comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 24 explained the source of the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי, the גמרא now brings in another statement from רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only names the speaker, and his content follows.
